A Map of the Arctic Ocean

2026-09-22 The Arctic Institute (Cryosphere Series 2026) Arctic Ocean, speculative map, ice retreat, territorial claims, shipping lanes, oil and gas exploration, wildlife migration, climate change, cartography, Arctic Institute
Read the source article

Quick summary

The Arctic Institute's Cryosphere Series 2026 features an artistic-scientific map of the Arctic Ocean that layers ice retreat, territorial claims, shipping routes, resource extraction zones, and wildlife migration into a single image, revealing the entangled forces reshaping the polar region.

Key takeaways

  • The map is an artistic tool constructed from scientific data, bringing together environmental change, political power, ecological life, human history, language, and territorial questions in one image
  • It layers Arctic ice boundaries, territorial claims, existing and proposed shipping lanes, oil and gas prospecting areas, and wildlife migration routes (birds and whales)
  • By assigning each trace an equal graphic value, the map proposes an understanding of the Arctic Ocean as an interconnected system rather than a collection of separate domains
  • The map includes linguistic regions, connecting human cultural geography to physical and political geography
  • Part of The Arctic Institute's Cryosphere Series 2026, the map functions as a tool for drawing connections between past and future trajectories of transformation
